original_question: Does the free group F_2 have finite centerpole numbers c_r^0(F_2) for every integer r?
target_in_paper: Section 11, Problem 11.4: "Has the free group F_2 finite centerpole numbers c_r^0(F_2) for all r in N?"
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's actual target very closely: it asks about the free group F_2, uses the paper's centerpole notation c_r^0(F_2), and asks the exact finiteness question for all numbers of colors. This is essentially the official formulation of Problem 11.4.
missing_details: Replace "for every integer r" by the paper's quantifier "for all r in N" (positive integers / natural numbers).
State that F_2 is the free group on two generators.
Unpack the notation c_r^0(F_2): it is the 0-centerpole number of the symmetry measure space (F_2, asdim, S).
Specify that S is the family of central symmetries of F_2.
Spell out what symmetry with respect to c means in group language: a subset A is symmetric with respect to c if A = c A^{-1} c.

Explain that c_r^0(F_2) is the least size of a finite set C of centers such that every r-coloring chi:F_2->r has a monochromatic subset A symmetric with respect to some c in C and having asymptotic dimension at least 0.

Because finite subsets have asymptotic dimension -1 in this setup, note that the requirement asdim(A) >= 0 is equivalent here to A being infinite; since F_2 is discrete, no extra Borel/measurability restriction is needed.
refined_question: Let F_2 be the free group on two generators, viewed as the symmetry measure space (F_2, asdim, S) with S the family of central symmetries. For each r in N, is the 0-centerpole number c_r^0(F_2) finite; equivalently, does there exist a finite set C subseteq F_2 such that every r-coloring chi:F_2->r contains an infinite monochromatic subset A subseteq F_2 with A = c A^{-1} c for some c in C?
equivalent_formulation: For every r in N, does there exist a finite family of central symmetries of F_2 such that every r-coloring of F_2 contains an infinite monochromatic subset symmetric with respect to one of those central symmetries?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's specific noncommutative-group question in Section 11, not the broader preceding Problem 11.3. Section 10 introduces the general centerpole numbers c_r^lambda(X), and Section 11 specializes this framework to groups equipped with the asymptotic-dimension measure and central symmetries, yielding the notation c_r^0(G). Problem 11.4 then asks exactly whether c_r^0(F_2) is finite for every r in N. The nearby context also records the only explicit partial information mentioned there, namely that c_2^0(F_2) <= 4 and the sharper follow-up Problem 11.5 asking whether c_2^0(F_2) is 4, 3, or 2. To make the question stand-alone, the main missing pieces are the meaning of c_r^0, the role of central symmetry, and the fact that in this group-asdim setting the superscript 0 corresponds to asking for an infinite monochromatic symmetric subset.
